meta.teaser: He started at age 4 at his dad's tennis club and never stopped smiling.

page.title: How Carlos Alcaraz became world No. 1 at 19
page.sub: The story of Carlos Alcaraz, Spain's tennis superstar
page.bigIdea: Alcaraz plays his best when he's having fun. He says he can't play well unless he's enjoying himself.

cards.title: He started at age 4
cards.front: Carlos grew up in El Palmar, a small town in Spain.
cards.back: His dad was a coach at the local tennis club, so Carlos started hitting balls at age 4. The club became his second home.
cards.tryit: Think back: what's the earliest thing you remember about tennis?

cards.title: A champion chose to coach him
cards.front: At 15, he moved to train with Juan Carlos Ferrero.
cards.back: Ferrero was a former world No. 1. He turned down top pros to coach teenage Carlos. They worked together for seven years.
cards.tryit: Ask your coach what one thing would most improve your game.

cards.title: Youngest No. 1 ever
cards.front: In 2022 he won the US Open at 19.
cards.back: That win made him world No. 1 at 19 years old, the youngest man ever. A year earlier he was ranked No. 32.
cards.tryit: Write down one big tennis goal and the first small step toward it.

cards.title: The magic drop shot
cards.front: His drop shot is famous for being almost impossible to reach.
cards.back: Former champion Andy Roddick called it the best in tennis history. Carlos hits huge forehands, then suddenly plays it soft.
cards.tryit: Practice 20 drop shots this week. Mix them in after hard shots.

cards.title: Fun is his secret weapon
cards.front: Alcaraz smiles a lot on court, even in big matches.
cards.back: He wants to win, but also to try new shots and entertain the crowd. Enjoying it helps him play his best.
cards.tryit: In your next match, try one creative shot just for fun.
